commitResults.messageTitle: Use varargs for task command words
commitResults.messageBody: Allow task constructors to accept a variable number of parsed command words while retaining compatibility with existing array-based callers.
Integrate the varargs task-constructor API after Checkstyle and test verification.
Provide a functional FXML-based GUI with a separate launcher, connect it to existing command and storage behavior, and retain the text interface for automated testing.

commitResults.messageTitle: Document task invariants with Java assertions
commitResults.messageBody:
Task operations rely on a valid occupied prefix and well-formed task state. Document these programmer-controlled assumptions with Java assert statements so violations fail close to their source when assertions are enabled.

Add focused tests for invalid task state and descriptions, while preserving user-facing validation through the existing exceptions.

Agents need a single repository-level source of truth for coding and Git
standards. Without an explicit requirement, conventions can be applied
inconsistently across tasks.

Require agents to review and follow the SE-EDU Java and Git guides.
Add verification steps for Java changes and commit messages, while
preserving exact identifiers required by course increments.

TaskLoader.addTask handles validation, dispatch, task mutation, and
response formatting in one long conditional. Mixing these abstraction
levels makes the command flow difficult to scan and extend.

Move command-specific work into focused methods and use a switch for
dispatch. This keeps the public entry point and dispatcher short while
preserving command behavior and response text.

StoredTaskLoader.load reads the file, validates commands, and tracks
state changes. It also prints results in the same method, hiding the
main loading flow behind low-level validation details.

Extract file iteration, single-command validation, and result reporting
into focused methods. Guard clauses keep blank and valid commands out
of the error path, making the happy path easier to follow.

Main and MainWindow contain bare numeric values for the initial window
size, minimum dimensions, and exit delay. Their purpose is not apparent
at each use site and later adjustments could become inconsistent.

Replace the literals with descriptive constants near their owning
classes. This makes the interface settings explicit while keeping the
rendered sizes and timing unchanged.

Event validation combines missing markers, missing arguments, and an
incorrect marker order in one dense condition. Readers must reconstruct
several syntax rules at once to understand why a command is rejected.

Name each invalid condition and combine the booleans at the decision
point. Add coverage for every invalid structure so the clearer
expression preserves the existing command contract.

Deadline, Event, and TaskLoader each contain the same loop for locating
format markers in tokenized commands. Multiple copies make this small
parsing rule easy to change inconsistently.

Move marker lookup to a focused CommandWords utility and reuse it at
each call site. This gives the shared rule one implementation without
coupling task types to the command processor.

Finding and storing tasks transform the occupied range of the task
array. Index-based loops obscure the filtering and mapping intent.

Use stream pipelines to select and format matching tasks and stored
commands. Preserve task numbering, command order, and the existing file
format, with tests covering multiple matches and completion records.
Add Java assertions for task invariants

Use streams for task transformations

GitHub-hosted runners use locales that render AM/PM markers in
uppercase, while BenBot requires lowercase markers. This causes the new
cross-platform CI build to fail despite passing on the development
machine.

Specify the English display locale and fixed lowercase period markers.
This preserves the existing user-facing format on every supported
platform. Cover the morning marker with a regression test as well.
